name: Council Communism
summary: Council communism is a left-communist current from 1920s Germany and the Netherlands holding that workers should run production and society directly through councils of recallable delegates. It rejects vanguard parties, parliaments and traditional trade unions, and judged the Soviet Union a form of state capitalism.
scope: Anton Pannekoek, Herman Gorter and Otto Rühle and the KAPD, plus later writers such as Paul Mattick, on the evidence of Pannekoek's Workers' Councils and Party and Class. Excludes the National Bolshevik wing (Laufenberg, Wolffheim). Many social, cultural and foreign-policy statements were never addressed and are low-confidence inferences.

sources.usedFor: Confirming the tradition's main debates (party, parliamentarism, unions).

universal-healthcare.rationale: Pannekoek never discusses healthcare; free provision of needs by the producers' commonwealth implies it, though not via a state ministry.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage labor itself is the exploitative relation to be abolished, so reformist wage-floor measures are not a goal; inferred, since the text does not address minimum wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Pannekoek attributes crises to the anarchy of competitive production and wants conscious planning in its place.

public-ownership.rationale: Pannekoek calls public ownership a middle-class program of disguised capitalism; ownership must lie with the producers themselves.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation reform is a capitalist-state remedy that council communists see as secondary to abolishing class ownership; inferred.

unions-good.rationale: The KAPD and AAUD, the core of the movement, rejected trade unions outright as bureaucratic bodies tying workers to capitalism and replaced them with factory organisations.

property-fundamental.rationale: The goal is common ownership by the producers; private property in the means of production is the basis of exploitation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation by the capitalist state is reformism; the aim is workers' control of production, not tighter regulation of owners.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not a topic Pannekoek addresses; opposed to capitalist austerity but sceptical of state welfare, so a mild disagreement inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Common ownership by workers organized in factory councils is the core of Pannekoek's program.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; a state apparatus above the masses is distrusted, so mild disagreement inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The tradition has no documented position on drug policy and adherents have no common view.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; distrust of state apparatus and emphasis on open debate among workers suggests mild disagreement.

strong-leader.rationale: Pannekoek rejects leaders acting for the class; workers must free themselves, and leader-led revolution yields a new ruling group.

state-harmful.rationale: Council communists reject the state apparatus of parties and bureaucrats as a new ruling class, though councils exercise collective power in the transition.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented position; adherents favoured armed workers during revolution but not a gun policy.

empower-police-military.rationale: Standing armed forces are instruments of the ruling class; funding them is opposed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; no common view.

decide-locally.rationale: Power is built from the bottom up from workplace and local councils, with delegates bound by instructions from their groups.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; a classless society removes the social roots of crime, so rehabilitation is inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Not a focus of the tradition; the aim of a new society leads to rejecting traditional norms as foundations, inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: No documented position from the 1920s-30s texts; a modern left-communist would likely agree but this is inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from left-wing outlook.

more-religion-public.rationale: Marxist materialism treats religion as ideology that the workers' self-education will outgrow; larger public role opposed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Council communists emphasise class unity and doubt state-led remedies; adherents split between rejecting and supporting such measures.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; materialist emphasis on social circumstances suggests mild agreement.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Pannekoek treats nationalism as capitalist delusive talk of community; national preservation is not a goal.

gradual-change.rationale: Pannekoek expects a heavy and lengthy struggle culminating in workers seizing the factories, not reform through established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Workers are an international class; restricting immigration divides them along national lines.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed; UN-style bodies of states are not workers' bodies, so mild disagreement inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Capitalist competition is seen as the source of crises and war, so it is not a benefit; the aim is planned production.

nation-first.rationale: Pannekoek says capitalists use talk of national community while competing for world power; workers have no national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Military action by capitalist states is imperialist rivalry; adherents would not endorse it.

open-borders.rationale: Internationalist class solidarity points toward the end of borders, though the sources do not state it as a program.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; production for need rather than profit but no growth-limit doctrine.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; a modern council communist would see climate crisis as caused by capitalism but doubt state-led fixes; inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Pannekoek values technology under social control but not that it alone solves problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by the tradition.

revolution-justified.rationale: Pannekoek holds that only mass action seizing the factories can overthrow capital.

experts-over-public.rationale: Experts act as technical leaders without privileges; decisions rest with the workers.

central-planning.rationale: Council communists favour conscious planning but through councils from below; rule by a central bureaucracy is judged a new ruling class.

socialized-markets.rationale: Without a market for exchange, production is for direct consumption; market socialism is not endorsed.

land-value-tax.rationale: Single-tax reform leaves capitalist relations intact; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; reform of capitalism is secondary to abolishing it.

basic-income.rationale: Unconditional state payment is not addressed; Pannekoek links consumption initially to labor performance, with shares for those unable to work.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Investment is decided by the producers' councils, not by a state; state direction is state capitalism.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: National protection serves capitalist rivalry; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Common ownership of the means of production is the aim, not dispersal among small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Pannekoek says wages under public ownership remain exploitation and that labor will be counted directly in hours, with money fading.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; the aim is abolishing money and markets, not leaving money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies bargaining with employers tie workers to capital, the same objection as to trade unions.

one-party-rule.rationale: Pannekoek says party rule is a new ruling group and a contradiction of proletarian revolution.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Pannekoek places all authority in workers' councils of delegates; he does not discuss monarchy, but hereditary heads of state have no place in that scheme.

democracy-best.rationale: They support council democracy but call parliamentary democracy a sham, so the statement splits.

direct-votes.rationale: Delegates are bound by instructions from the groups that send them; direct decision in the workplace is central, though the system is delegate-based.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils of delegates, not parliaments, are the defining form of power in council communism.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no stated stance.

natural-rulers.rationale: Pannekoek's Workers' Councils holds that workers must decide together through their councils rather than follow leaders, which rules out a class of natural rulers; he does not take up the claim directly.

political-violence-never.rationale: Pannekoek expects a heavy struggle and capitalist resistance with all its powers.

war-builds-character.rationale: Pannekoek explains wars as rivalry among capitalist powers; he does not discuss war and national character, so rejection follows from that analysis.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed directly; separation consistent with materialism.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law is seen as a field of class contest, not divine order.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Protecting property for private profit is the capitalist order the council system replaces.

military-superiority.rationale: Great-power military competition is attributed to capitalism.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Internationalist class politics rejects ethnic national organisation; the National Bolshevik wing was a minority deviation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Pannekoek describes labor under capitalism as a constant silent war and law as a contest between exploiting and exploited classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Distribution by common ownership aims at ending exploitation, with shares for all including those unable to work.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; adherents oppose imperialism but reparations are not in the sources.

civilizational-union.rationale: Class, not civilization, is the basis of unity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Pannekoek sets solidarity and community of producers against capitalist profit-seeking.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; collectivist about production, but council communists stress self-determination and oppose subordination to authorities.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Pannekoek sees industrial production as the base of a future commonwealth under workers' control.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technology is valued but not disruption for its own sake.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Delegates and workers decide; bookkeeping is a task for workers' control, not rule by algorithms; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement aims at a new, classless society through revolution; restoring a past order is not discussed but runs against its goal.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pannekoek says capitalism must be beaten theoretically before materially, stressing theory; mild disagreement.

direct-action.rationale: The movement rejects parliaments and relies on mass strikes, factory seizures and councils.

means-match-ends.rationale: Pannekoek argues a party seizing power cannot bring a classless self-governed society; workers' self-activity is itself the means.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Pannekoek's programme assumes large-scale industrial production run in common by the producers; returning to foraging is never discussed.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Pannekoek says administration is a special task like hammering steel, though all workers conceive and decide together; full abolition is not stated.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Pannekoek says shares go to the unable too, while early consumption is coupled to work performance, so ultimate need-based distribution is implied.

production-for-use.rationale: Pannekoek contrasts capital's profit aim with providing life necessities as the aim of the new system.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Wages under any ownership remain exploitation in his account; profit arises from labor of producers.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: They accept working-class power through councils but reject party dictatorship; the statement's wording is split for them.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are split.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Pannekoek links war to competing capitalist powers fighting for world power.

taxation-theft.rationale: Collective provision is accepted; property of owners is not defended.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Class collectivity is central, though the framework emphasises self-determination of workers.

conscription.rationale: Standing armies are tools of the ruling class; workers' conscription for war is rejected.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Collective participation by councils is central, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The councils are meant to replace profit-driven rule and the state itself; running government like a firm is not discussed but runs against the programme.

positive-liberty.rationale: Freedom is tied to workers' control over their conditions of production, beyond non-interference.

media-academia-power.rationale: Real power lies with capital, in their analysis, not with media and academia.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Materialist view of social causes; adherents reject racial genetic explanation.

organic-representation.rationale: Councils of workplace delegates are class-based, not organic bodies of family and community; the statement is anti-party but corporatist.

total-state.rationale: Pannekoek rejects state or party direction of life as a new form of domination.

national-rebirth.rationale: The movement is internationalist; the National Bolshevik wing is a rejected minority.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Imperialist expansion is attributed to capitalism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: In Pannekoek's council system delegates carry instructions from below and can be recalled; feudal oaths are not discussed but are excluded by that model.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Pannekoek holds capitalism must be beaten theoretically; no explicit stance on knowledge neutrality.

single-common-good.rationale: Society is divided by class interests, so a single common good is not assumed under capitalism.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; internationalism opposes nationalist state projects.

revive-national-language.rationale: Nationalist cultural projects are not a goal; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Pannekoek says all workers conceive, devise and decide together in factory organization.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; market mechanism in education is opposed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic freedom in the sense of private property and markets is the basis of exploitation.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; authority is in councils, not rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Class is the unit; the sources treat nationalism as capitalist ideology.

force-without-un.rationale: Capitalist states' wars are imperialist and rejected.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Marxist materialism and the call for theoretical clarity point toward reason.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Pannekoek couples early consumption to labor performance but also shares for those unable; adherents split.

class-collaboration.rationale: Labor under capitalism is a constant silent war; collaboration with capital is rejected.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; no futurist or iconoclast position.

dominated-front.rationale: Class rather than national front is the basis; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: The working class is international; the National Bolshevik wing was a deviation.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to capital but not through legal bans on interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Council communists stress the unity of the whole working class; the sources do not discuss race law, so the answer follows from that principle.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Pannekoek says parliaments rule over constituents and public ownership is disguised capitalism, treating the state as a class instrument.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy theories of this kind are foreign to a class analysis.

proportional-representation.rationale: Pannekoek says parliaments are sham democracy whatever the electoral system.

national-mission.rationale: Pannekoek treats nationalism as a capitalist ideology dividing workers; national civilising missions follow as rejected though not discussed as such.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed in sources; left outlook suggests mild agreement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Parliamentarians are not true mandatories and parties are tools of ruling groups.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is not part of the tradition.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The sources say nothing on legal accountability for past state abuses; adherents have no distinctive position, so neutral.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The programme is common ownership administered by producers' councils, the opposite of a minimal state that guards property; the statement itself is not discussed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Egalitarian but the tradition focuses on class.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Pannekoek says the entrenched Western bourgeoisie requires mass seizure, linking to world revolution; stated by the tradition as internationalist.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The council-communist texts I read never discuss settler states; no position can be inferred from class analysis.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law is outside what the council-communist texts cover, so neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; free self-determination of workers inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; religious-based legal bans are unlikely to be endorsed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Council communists denounced the Soviet state as state capitalism with a new ruling class.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Self-rule by workers is central, though the liberal formulation is not theirs.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantile competition belongs to capitalist rivalry.

population-transfer.rationale: Follows from the movement's opposition to national division of workers; the sources do not discuss expelling minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Violent revolution accepted against capital; the libertarian statement does not fit.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Competition is blamed for crises; solidarity is central.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: State repression of parties is distrusted; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Opposition to rule by leaders, parties and capital fits freedom as non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Councils combine legislating and executing in delegates bound by instructions; checks between state bodies are not the model.

vanguard-party.rationale: Pannekoek says a revolutionary party leading the class substitutes a ruling group for self-emancipation.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Class solidarity aims at working-class interests but via workers' self-rule.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Mass strikes and factory occupations are the method of revolution.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Pannekoek attributes poverty to capitalist exploitation; he does not engage the population argument directly.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; delegates are mandated and replaceable, not chosen by lot.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Party dictatorship and state repression are rejected.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; capitalist state measures are seen as insufficient.

party-controls-media.rationale: Party control is a new form of rule rejected by Pannekoek.

party-commands-army.rationale: In Party and Class Pannekoek condemns parties that 'seize power for themselves' and the Communist 'party dictatorship', so no party should command the armed power of society.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Delegates who are workers, bound to instructions, without privileges; experts without privileges; pay cap inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Pannekoek favours loose fluid groups of opinion over disciplined parties; binding discipline suspected as party rigidity.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The EU is a capitalist union; not addressed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Pannekoek criticises systems where command passes to a leader or central government and puts decisions in councils of mandated delegates; he does not address heads of state or legislatures directly.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not something the tradition addresses; neutral by indifference.

clerical-rule.rationale: Pannekoek treats law "sanctified by religion" as cover for class rule, which bears on religion's role but not on rule by clergy specifically; disagreement follows from council sovereignty.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Pannekoek attributes wars to competing capitalist powers, so workers should not support them; defeatism itself is Leninist and not stated.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Open debate in workers' groups is valued, censorship rejected as party intolerance.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Delegates are replaceable by their groups, which implies term accountability.

recall-officials.rationale: Delegates can be recalled at any time in council systems.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Opposes capitalist alliances but also military withdrawal is not a documented plank, so split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Common ownership, not family property, is the aim.

people-in-arms.rationale: Armed workers in revolution are part of the tradition's picture, though not stated explicitly in my sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The sources give no view on the educated and ordinary life; Pannekoek's own scientific career cuts against hostility.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural ranking is not discussed in the sources, so no position is documented.

death-penalty.rationale: Not directly addressed; inferred from rejection of state coercive apparatus and humane outlook.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not a topic in the texts; adherents have no shared line on censorship of this kind.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, so no position can be documented.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The sources are silent on social conformity; neutral rather than guessing.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-imperialist; the topic itself not addressed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Political reform without ownership change is judged disguised capitalism.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Parliamentary assemblies are rejected as sham democracy in favour of councils.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: They criticised the Soviet Union for exactly this and called it state capitalism.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: State aid between capitalist countries is not discussed; the tradition has no documented position.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Council system has no head of state; elections within parliaments are rejected.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Money is to be abolished; not addressed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Common ownership aims at the common benefit but they reject capitalist property outright, rather than limiting it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Gorter, Pannekoek and the 1933 Theses on Bolshevism called the USSR state capitalist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is anachronistic for the 1920s-40s texts, so neutral.

collective-defense.rationale: Military alliances are of capitalist powers.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Territorial disputes between states are not addressed in the sources read; neutral.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The tradition distrusts the state apparatus but also religion, so adherents are indifferent or split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; no head of state in a council system.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; opposed to national military force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy within larger states is not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

character-from-environment.rationale: Pannekoek cites Owen and Marx on circumstances changed by struggle.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic and untouched by the tradition's texts, so neutral.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Pannekoek lodges power in workers' councils alone; mixing rule by the few and the many is not addressed but has no place in the model.

leader-cult.rationale: Pannekoek attacks parties for training 'loyal and unquestioning members' and insists workers must 'think, act, and decide for themselves', the opposite of venerating a leader.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law is not discussed in the sources; no position documented.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: They see a party-ruled society as a new class society, so class conflict persists; the Maoist framing is not theirs.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; Pannekoek focused on industrial Western workers.

refugee-return.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; internationalism leans sympathetic, but no stated position.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Class, not ancestry, is the basis of unity.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not discussed by the tradition; internationalism opposes ethnic nationalism but no stated position on return rights.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Outside the tradition, which is internationalist and class-based; no position on minority cultural institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Internationalist class politics oppose founding separate homelands and favour joint struggle where people live; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: As Marxists, Pannekoek grounds social change in the development of production and the workers' conditions, with ideas following material change.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust aims to preserve competitive capitalism, which they want abolished; concentration is seen as a step toward socialization. Inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Never addressed; they oppose state capitalism but also want no private rescue, so neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: They reject bourgeois courts and parliaments but favour council majority rule; mixed, inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Never addressed; council delegates are recallable by electors and not allocated by quota, inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Internationalism and the world revolution, with councils linked across borders, oppose a closed national or colonial bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Treaties between capitalist states are not their route to workers' emancipation; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Pannekoek envisions production by free associated producers motivated by social duty rather than wages, though he emphasises labor-time accounting.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Pannekoek and the KAPD insisted that the revolution must be the self-emancipation of the masses, rejecting minority putsches and vanguards.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Abolition of classes and privilege is the goal and hereditary titles are feudal remnants, inferred from that.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Councils are internationalist and class-based, so a nation-centred curriculum is not a goal; inferred from the rejection of national loyalty, since Pannekoek does not discuss schooling.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Emancipation must be the workers' own act, and the tradition opposed imperial rule as a feature of capitalism; no ruling people can free another.

patriotic-education.rationale: The workers' movement is internationalist and has no stake in national loyalty; teaching pride in flag and anthem serves the capitalist state.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Class, not race, is the dividing line and rights are universal among producers, so race-based preferences are not a council aim; inferred, as the texts do not address them.

public-money-creation.rationale: Pannekoek wants production planned by the producers themselves, not money policy run by a state body, which he would see as state capitalism; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Pannekoek holds that capitalism's crises and anarchy of production are not curable by reform and drive the system toward its end through workers' action.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Internationalism and opposition to imperialism rule out building influence over former imperial lands; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: The programme is world revolution of the working class, not national economic withdrawal; inferred from internationalism.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The council view treats the working class as one international exploited class with common interests, against any split between privileged and exploited workers.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Private control of workplaces is abolished in favour of common ownership by producers, so owners' discretion to exclude is not defended; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Council communists see legal guarantees under the capitalist state as bourgeois forms; rights are secured by workers' direct control and recall; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Internationalist and anti-imperialist, council communists saw imposed borders as capitalist artefacts, though they rejected nationalism; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Council delegates are elected and recallable, and there is no hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Councils decide by majority of delegates, who are bound by instructions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Delegates can be recalled at once for breaking their mandate, but bourgeois constitutional law was not their frame; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Council communists reject parliamentarism outright, and the KAPD refused to take part in elections.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; a humane materialist outlook suggests it, inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no stated view.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: They reject charity from the privileged and want workers to free themselves by abolishing class.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Self-emancipation requires workers' own mass action in councils.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marxist view that capitalist culture serves capital; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Pannekoek stresses the spiritual and ideological hold of the ruling class as well as force; inferred from his framework.

native-born-offices.rationale: Internationalist; the only division is class.

party-own-road.rationale: They broke with the Comintern's Moscow line and rejected direction by any party.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Internationalist world revolution outweighs national self-reliance; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The only division is class, not ancestry.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: They saw fascism as capitalism and rejected popular-front anti-fascism and constitutions; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: They condemned Soviet state capitalism and fascism but explained both by class analysis, so adherents differ on equating them; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Materialist reading of slave economy conflict; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred; they have no stake in preserving old national symbols.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Class, not gender, is the frame; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Class, not gender, is the frame; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The council form is meant as a universal workers' system, not a regional one; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army is an instrument of the ruling class; workers must arm themselves instead.

paid-care-work.rationale: Pannekoek wants wages abolished for accounted labour time, so recognised yes but paid wages no; inferred and split.

filial-duty.rationale: Family duty was not a council-communist topic; adherents have no settled view, so this is an inference.

office-by-exam.rationale: Councils fill posts by election and recall of workers, and distrust a specialist expert stratum as a new ruling class.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and opposition to national capitalist economies, which includes state protection of firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the tradition stress on individual emancipation and rejection of traditional authority.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Councils of delegates who are directly bound by and recallable by those who elected them are the core of the doctrine.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The Pannekoek council economy replaces wage labour and market finance with social planning, so private pension funds are opposed.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Means of production, including land, are held in common by the councils; the use-only tenure detail is inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The KAPD rejected parliaments as a bourgeois device, so budget approval by one is not a goal.

single-official-language.rationale: Internationalist and hostile to nationalism, so a compulsory single language is unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Internationalism and rejection of nationalism; inferred, since land law was not addressed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Focus was on class; adherents would see unequal outcomes as a product of capitalism but not necessarily legal discrimination. Inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Production for need rather than profit and critique of capitalist waste imply a critical view of consumerism; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Opposed capitalist and Soviet state power and held that workers must emancipate themselves, so arming proxies for a state is not endorsed; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Judged the USSR a form of state capitalism and condemned its imperial control; inferred for bloc interventions.

corporate-influence.rationale: Council communism holds capital rules society and the bourgeois state serves it, so lobbying and money in politics are one expression of that class rule, though it wants the system replaced, not reformed.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: a stateless internationalist current distrusts state control over who funds organisations, though it would also oppose capitalist-funded influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and rejection of state direction of private life; it never addressed population policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: it wants property held in common by the producers' councils, not restricted by local authorities, and rejects nationalist closure; never directly addressed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: it aims to abolish wage labour and the state, so a state employer of last resort would be seen as state capitalism, though all able members would work in the commonwealth.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: it treats bourgeois parliamentary democracy as a capitalist form and war as a product of imperialist capital, so spreading it would not bring peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of the state as an instrument of class rule, though it expects binding decisions inside the councils.

non-intervention.rationale: Adherents opposed imperialist wars and state intervention but backed international working-class solidarity and revolution, so the absolute claim is split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Council communists rejected craft and trade unions and urged organisation by the workplace and industry, as in the AAUD's unitary organisations.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A class analysis locating power in capital and the state leaves no room for ethnic conspiracy theories, which Marxists reject as a diversion from class struggle.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist view of the family as shaped by property and the aim of withering away of state functions; Pannekoek did not discuss it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: councils of recallable delegates answerable to workers require open reporting back, though a legal right against a state was not its framing.

local-production.rationale: Pannekoek's council economy plans production through federated councils on a wide scale, so it implies neither localism nor its opposite.

informal-organisation.rationale: It rejected permanent parties but built formal council and workplace organisations with recallable delegates and federations, not small informal affinity groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and rejection of the bourgeois nation-state; the Marxist-excluded National Bolshevik wing would differ.

religious-nation.rationale: A materialist, internationalist current that rejects nations defined by religion and the nation-state itself.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Council communism rejects hierarchy among states as among classes and is internationalist; inferred, as the texts do not address tribute systems.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Internationalist solidarity of workers implies pooling across regions rather than regional hoarding; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Marxist core is common ownership of the means of production by the producers, not of personal belongings; Pannekoek has the producers own and run production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Adherents are communists who hold that council communism is the working-class goal; they condemn the USSR as state capitalism, not communism itself.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Production and services are to be run by the workers directly through councils, so private providers are not a goal; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Marxist tradition treats religion as a product of social conditions that fades with their change; inferred, as the cited texts do not discuss religion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: In the Marxist view capitalism developed the productive forces and the working class that make communism possible; inferred, not checked against the cited texts.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxist-derived view that class and economic structure shape social subordination; inferred, as council communists wrote little on gender.

socialized-care.rationale: Socialising domestic work is a classic Marxist aim and fits communal organisation; inferred, not addressed by Pannekoek.

purge-loanwords.rationale: An internationalist movement with no interest in linguistic nationalism; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Opposes the state as an instrument of class rule and sides with oppressed groups, but treaties are not discussed; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Council communism envisions society-wide federated workers councils rather than small isolated communes; inferred from the council system in Workers Councils.

majority-settlement.rationale: Strongly internationalist and hostile to nationalist state policy; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rejects capitalism and the Soviet model alike, but sees genuine communism run by workers councils as the sound basis, so disagrees that a separate third course is needed; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Pannekoek's internationalism rejects national and religious claims over land; never addressed directly, so inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: A materialist, internationalist left tradition would reject denial; not discussed in the sources, so inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's anti-authoritarian emphasis on workers' self-emancipation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Pannekoek rejects a ruling party but accepts that the councils defend themselves against counter-revolution; never addressed in general, so inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not addressed; a materialist, anti-authoritarian movement would oppose state punishment of belief, inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Council communists opposed imperialism and capitalism's exploitation of colonies as part of the class struggle.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as indifferent to a religious duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religion's place in government was not discussed; inferred from rejecting rule by any ruling elite.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Pannekoek's central idea is workers' councils in which workers decide production and society directly.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The movement centres class but did not theorise intersectionality; inferred as split.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the egalitarian emancipatory aim of communism.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the stress on individual freedom and self-determination.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Council communists see class divide between workers and capital as the basic political fact and reject cross-class compromise.

alienated-labor.rationale: Pannekoek follows Marx in seeing wage labour as exploitation that denies workers control over production.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the internationalist rejection of nationalism and cultural exclusion.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred from the materialist rejection of religious and ruling authority; authority lies in the workers.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's secular stance.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the workers' side of the labour question.

social-market-economy.rationale: The movement wants commodity production and wage labour replaced by council-run production, rejecting both market and state control.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed in detail; inferred from opposition to standing state institutions and preference for armed workers.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the strong egalitarian aim of communism.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Council communists opposed both rival imperialist blocs, as in the KAPD's stance; inferred for modern policy.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inherited office contradicts rule by recallable delegates and the rejection of hierarchy and leaders that define the tradition.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Council communists want banks and money abolished in a planned, council-run economy, so mutual banks are a reformist halfway house; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Opposed to capitalist institutions in general, they would back refusing lender conditions, though they reject national states as the unit; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Political power belongs to workers' councils, and wealth qualifications run directly against the working-class self-rule in Pannekoek's account.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The tradition did not address the link; its anti-hierarchy outlook is compatible but it was not a theme, so no clear position; inferred.

reification.rationale: Reification is a Marxist idea the council tradition shares in its critique of capitalism's hidden social relations; inferred, not stated in these sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: As Marxists they see formal bourgeois freedoms as limited by class power, though they reject a party-controlled press as the remedy; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: They want councils to govern directly and distrust bourgeois legal forms, but did not speak to decree versus standing law; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Proletarian internationalism rules out ethnic or racial qualifications for taking part in councils.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; direct delegate democracy would extend to online tools if they stayed under workers' control; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Recallable, instructed delegates need open proceedings so workers can check them; inferred from the council model.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: A secular materialist current opposed to dividing workers by religion would reject legal limits on marriage; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Dividing workers by religion cuts against class unity, so such boycotts are rejected; inferred from internationalism.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Council communism wants decisions made by mandated, recallable delegates from workplace councils, which is a form of direct democracy, but it says nothing about choosing people by lot. Inferred and split.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The texts concern class organization and do not address religious law; religion is not a topic the profile covers. Neutral inference.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The tradition holds that concentrated capital gives a ruling class power over workers, and that workers' self-rule requires ending it.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the egalitarian outlook and opposition to standing armed forces.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Religion is seen as an ideology workers will outgrow through self-education, but the tradition rejects state-imposed doctrine; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the tradition treats the state as a class instrument to be replaced, but how safety would be organised is not specified.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Councils are class bodies run by delegates and the tradition does not address communal power-sharing; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The councils are meant to organise social production and need collectively, so reliance on private charity is inferred as opposed.

term-limits.rationale: Council delegates are rotated and recallable, which implies limits on tenure; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Delegates are bound and recallable by those who elected them, which is close to revocable delegation, though not by policy area.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no basis for a position.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarianism and materialist hostility to clerical hierarchies.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the egalitarian, anti-hierarchy outlook.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Councils are built on workers where they live and work, and the movement is internationalist and class-based, so excluding resident workers from local voice is not implied; inferred, not discussed.

rent-control.rationale: Rent caps are a state reform inside capitalism; the council view aims at abolishing the wage and property relations altogether. Inferred, not discussed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Production is to be run in common by the producers, so private monopolies on knowledge fit poorly; inferred, as the texts do not address patents.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Council communism rejects militarism and state-led, party-led organisation of the working class, which must emancipate itself; drilled national youth movements contradict this.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: An internationalist current opposed to nationalism and the arms race; inferred, as nuclear basing is not discussed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Internationalist and anti-militarist stance implies opposition to foreign military bases; inferred, not discussed.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and hostility to imperial and state violence; the specific practice of formal recognition by governments is not addressed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The aim is abolition of wage labour and exploitation, with production run by the producers, so income from ownership is rejected in principle.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The current accepted revolutionary class violence and civil war, so an absolute ban on killing is not part of it; inferred, not discussed.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Council communism is internationalist and rejects nationalism (it excludes the National Bolshevik wing), so a timeless national essence is rejected.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed by the movement and no settled position can be inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed by the movement and no settled position can be inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Rejects nationalism and the glorification of the state's wars, treating them as class wars; honouring national martyrs runs against this.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Historical-materialist analysis grounds politics in class conflict and material conditions, not a spiritual contest of good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and the rejection of national homelands as organising principles; not discussed.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement holds that the working class's own self-organisation, not nation-building, drives change, and it rejects nationalism; cultural renewal of a nation as a precondition is alien to it.

god-not-male.rationale: Materialist and secular current; the question of God's description is not addressed and is not a concern.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is secular and took no position on religious texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Internationalist and class-based, it rejects economic privilege for any national group over others; the question is framed in nationalist terms it opposes.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Rejects nationalism and the national self-determination programme; councils are formed on class lines, not by merging territories for a people.

independent-unions.rationale: Pannekoek wanted organisations run by their members rather than officials, so unions would be independent of any state or party; inferred, as he rejected unions altogether.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Council communists held that the Soviet system was state capitalism because workers lacked power, so socialism requires workers' own rule.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Common ownership of production run by the councils implies public control of essentials; not discussed for local services specifically.

second-chamber.rationale: Council communists rejected parliaments in favour of the council system, so a second chamber alongside one is excluded.

municipal-property.rationale: Production is to be owned by the workers' councils, not by the locality, the private owner or the state; the locality is not the owner.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Pannekoek's higher councils are made of bound, recallable delegates who coordinate while the base decides.

family-wage.rationale: Abolition of wage labour is the goal, so a family wage is not a council communist aim; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The sources never address this, and nothing in the ideology's principles points clearly either way, so it is left neutral.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The sources never address this, and nothing in the ideology's principles points clearly either way, so it is left neutral.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The sources never address this, and nothing in the ideology's principles points clearly either way, so it is left neutral.

online-anonymity.rationale: The sources never address this, and nothing in the ideology's principles points clearly either way, so it is left neutral.

person-over-state.rationale: Emancipation of the individual worker by their own act is central; inferred, not stated as a general principle.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Marxist materialism leaves little room for spiritual needs as a political aim; inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: No parliament in the system, so the question does not arise; not addressed.

gm-crops.rationale: The sources never address this, and nothing in the ideology's principles points clearly either way, so it is left neutral.

dense-cities.rationale: The sources never address this, and nothing in the ideology's principles points clearly either way, so it is left neutral.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement was class-internationalist and opposed national and racial divisions among workers.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from class internationalism.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Council communists opposed imperialist war but not defence as such; not addressed.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Council communists were internationalists who saw the working class, not nations, as the political subject; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: Councils are organised by workplace and class; separate religious electorates would divide the working class, so this is inferred as strongly rejected.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Pannekoek and Gorter held nationalism to be bourgeois ideology, and a partition plot narrative is a nationalist frame; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Education is part of the producers' commonwealth's free provision of needs; Pannekoek never discusses tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Never addressed; council communists rejected market mechanisms and held that producers should regulate production directly, so a tax is inferred as unlikely.

future-generations.rationale: Not discussed; a society run by associated producers for need is inferred to care for the Earth.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Never addressed; class is the council communist category and gender-difference claims were not part of it.

arms-reduction.rationale: Council communists opposed militarism as an instrument of capitalist states; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Rank-and-file control of workers' councils implies openness, and open diplomacy was a standard left demand; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Council communists rejected the state as the manager of the economy (state capitalism), so state capital controls are not endorsed, yet they oppose capital; inferred and split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: councils rest on armed workers rather than a state army, but the sources do not discuss a state arms monopoly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the movement's internationalism and class self-emancipation; the sources do not discuss refusal of orders.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Council communists rejected traditional trade unions as binding workers to capitalism, so union bargaining is not their route.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: wage labour is the relation to abolish, so subsidising low wages is a reformist measure.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: capitalist state budget rules are not a concern of the producers' commonwealth; not discussed in the sources.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: they seek world revolution rather than reform of capitalist international rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Council communists hold that workers must replace the bourgeois state apparatus with their own councils rather than take it over.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Pannekoek wants conscious planning by the councils in place of market anarchy, so a free mix of systems is not the aim.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from the critique of capital accumulation; valuing nature as capital is not discussed.

sacred-nation.rationale: Council communism is internationalist and class-based, so the nation as a sacred community is rejected.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: relief within capitalism is a reformist palliative; not discussed.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: the analysis is of class rather than region; not discussed.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from Marxist historical materialism, which treats human nature as shaped by social conditions; not discussed.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: they want workers to run their own press and organisations, not state-funded bodies; not discussed.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Council communists were materialist Marxists who treated religion as ideology; inferred from that materialism, as the sources do not discuss it.

farm-price-support.rationale: State price guarantees and credit would run through a state apparatus and keep commodity production; inferred, since Pannekoek wants council-run planning of production instead.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's internationalism and hostility to state power; the texts predate or ignore the question.

workers-own-party.rationale: Pannekoek holds that workers' own organs are councils and that parties acting for the class lead to party rule, so a permanent workers' party is not the vehicle.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's universalist emancipation of the oppressed; not addressed in the sources.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from equality of all producers; private inheritance of land is not a council-communist concern, so this is weakly held.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The sources never address language classification and adherents have no shared view.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: harms would be handled by conscious social planning by the councils, not by private suits or by state agencies.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Pannekoek's council system gives lawmaking to recallable delegates of workers and leaves no formal place for hereditary or customary authority.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Ecology is not addressed in the sources; adherents would stress democratic social control of production over either side.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's rejection of state coercion and punitive institutions; not discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and opposition to state compulsion; not discussed.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Council communists rejected traditional trade unions altogether as bureaucratic, so the question of compulsory membership never arose in their terms.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: they rejected parliaments and state apparatus, and would see state identification rules as irrelevant to or restricting worker participation.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Marxist treatment of religion as a private matter; not discussed by Pannekoek.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: They rejected parliamentary democracy and held that real democracy is workers' councils of recallable delegates, not elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the general Marxist and libertarian-left outlook; not discussed.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from commitment to workers' self-organisation and free communication.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: they sought to abolish wage labor, and a cash scheme would only manage capitalist poverty.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred: councils are open to all workers, though they rejected parliaments, so voting and office-holding in the state are not their focus.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not discussed; Marxists see religion as ideology of class society, not primarily as a cause of women's oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist materialist outlook that treats such categories as products of society; not discussed.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: they opposed state apparatus and would leave equality to workers' self-organisation, not ministries.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from the aim of common ownership of the means of production, which leaves no place for first-claim private title to resources.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to state institutions and to bourgeois law, so adherents would not look to state-run international courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Marxist materialism of Pannekoek and Gorter, who treated religion as ideology.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the goal of full equal participation of all workers in the councils.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Council communists called the Soviet Union state capitalism and opposed a bureaucracy ruling over workers, so defending such a state is rejected.

indirect-election.rationale: The council system is a pyramid in which higher councils are made up of delegates from lower ones, recallable at any time.

national-church-status.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the rejection of institutions standing above the workers' own organisation.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; the current's internationalism opposes nationalism, but it never took up minority autonomy within states.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed; internationalist class politics gives no stated position on territorial plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed; rejection of nationalism and of state frontiers leaves no stated view on colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the aim of abundance through socialised production; simple living is not a council-communist theme.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the internationalist opposition to national exclusion by territory.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of standing armies and the arming of workers generally, with no gender distinction.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from its internationalist Marxism, which treats the working class rather than the nation as the unit of struggle.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its workers-democratic commitments and opposition to repressive state power.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic; the current died out before the issue arose, and it viewed all powers as capitalist.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and rejection of nationalist politics.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its demand that production be owned and managed collectively by the workers councils.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its collectivist view that workers jointly control production rather than each owning their own labour as property.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred as a Marxist concern that consumption taxes fall on workers; the sources do not address taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from its aim of replacing welfare provision with workers self-management; targeting is not discussed.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Split by the statement: it rejects parties as intermediaries, but also rejects any leader above the councils.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to capitalist class rule, including state-capitalist privileges.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from its materialist, class-based politics, which does not organise on religious lines.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from its modernist Marxism and its lack of interest in a return to ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from its Marxist support for the equality of women; the sources do not address divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred as split: it is internationalist and favours workers rather than national control of resources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from its aim of common ownership of production, where distribution follows workers' collective decisions rather than entitlements.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of reformist measures that manage capitalism instead of abolishing it.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred as class-first, but the sources do not discuss racial disadvantage, so the answer is left neutral.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: It treats law as an instrument of class rule rather than a moral question; the natural-law wording is not addressed.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from Marxist views of technology freeing labour; Pannekoek's councils aim at workers controlling production, not at less work.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and rejection of rival national blocs, including Soviet power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Pannekoek writes as a Marxist for whom workers produce all value and capital exploits their labour, the basis of the council case.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from the KAPD's internationalism and rejection of national unity; the wing that combined them was excluded.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from its class-only analysis; cultural identity politics post-dates the tradition.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: It rejects party rule over the working class and called the Soviet system state capitalism, so a party-led market socialism is the opposite of its aim.

missingStatements.text: Delegates to a decision-making body should be bound by instructions from the people who elected them and replaceable at any time.
missingStatements.rationale: Pannekoek says council delegates carry specific instructions, report back, and can be replaced, the defining mechanism of the council system.

missingStatements.text: Existing trade unions bind workers to capitalism and should be replaced by organization built on the workplace itself.
missingStatements.rationale: Pannekoek contrasts unions, where officials devise and members vote, with shop organization where workers decide, and the KAPD and AAUD fought traditional unions.
missingStatements.declined: Covered by unions-good and workers-councils, which council communism already answers; the anti-union claim is the same position seen from the other side.

missingStatements.text: Revolutionary parties should not take power on behalf of the working class, whose emancipation must be its own act.
missingStatements.rationale: Pannekoek argues that a party seizing power replaces one ruling group with another, and the working class can only be freed by itself.

notes: Council communists differ from other Marxists mainly on organization: they favour councils over parties, unions and parliaments. Many cultural questions are not documented. Dictatorship of the proletariat, central planning and distribution by need are answered with varying confidence.
